sections.heading: A — Exam authority for the driving responsibilities section (Tennessee Class D knowledge test)
sections.markdown:
## A — Exam authority for the driving responsibilities section (Tennessee Class D knowledge test)
Issuer: the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security, Driver Services Division, publishes the Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual and takes written comments on it [A01].
Edition statement: the manual says its information was current as of July 1, 2022, and later law, rule or policy changes override anything outdated in it [A01].
Freshness: that content date is old and no issuer page confirms it as the current edition, so every fact here is held under freshness debt until rechecked (verify TN-RESP-A-FRESH).
Knowledge test: a multiple-choice exam drawn from Sections B and C of the manual, split roughly equally across traffic signs and signals, safe driving principles, rules of the road, and drugs and alcohol [A02].
Format: given on computerized testing machines at Driver Service Centers, with Spanish, Korean and Japanese versions where computerized testing is offered, and oral tests by appointment for applicants who cannot read [A02].
Vision: a screening of at least 20/40 in each eye and in both eyes together, with or without corrective lenses, comes before any license or permit [A02].
Retake rule: after failing any knowledge test you must wait at least one day before trying again [A03].
Question count, passing score and time limit: the manual states none of them, so all three stay unknown and are never shown to learners (verify TN-RESP-A-EXAM).
This section feeds the knowledge test: this chapter sits in Section B of the manual, from which the knowledge test is drawn, and most closely matches the rules of the road area; it covers the Problem Driver Pointer System, the grounds for suspension and revocation, license surrender and hearings, address changes, the Non-Resident Violator Compact, reinstatement, the point system and its chart, restricted licenses, medical review and re-examination, financial responsibility, crash reporting and conduct at a crash scene; its sample questions target the crash report deadline, what to do when passing a crash you cannot help with, and the grounds for suspension.
Practice quizzes follow the product mastery policy from the learning loop, which is not an official exam threshold.

sections.heading: B — Audience, level and prerequisites: driving responsibilities
sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: driving responsibilities
Audience: every first-time Tennessee Class D or learner permit applicant, and especially drivers under eighteen, who face lower point thresholds and school-related license loss.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the grounds for losing a license [A01], the point thresholds [A02] and the crash reporting duties [A05] decide whether a new license survives its first mistakes.
Level: rule recall with many deadlines, point values and dollar thresholds, plus procedure recall for crash scenes; moderate to high load.
Prerequisites: the license and graduated license chapters, and the alcohol chapter for DUI, implied consent and under-twenty-one rules.

sections.heading: C — Driving responsibilities: the Problem Driver Pointer System, losing your license, surrender and hearings, address changes, the Non-Resident Violator Compact, the point system, restricted licenses, medical review, financial responsibility, reporting crashes and what to do at a crash scene
sections.markdown:
## C — Driving responsibilities: the Problem Driver Pointer System, losing your license, surrender and hearings, address changes, the Non-Resident Violator Compact, the point system, restricted licenses, medical review, financial responsibility, reporting crashes and what to do at a crash scene
Knowledge domain: the duties that come with a Tennessee license — how out-of-state problems block a license, what gets a license suspended or revoked, how surrender, hearings and address changes work, how points add up toward suspension, when a restricted license is possible, how medical conditions are reviewed, what proof of financial responsibility means, when and how crashes must be reported, and how to act at a crash scene.

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Before issuing a license, Tennessee uses the Problem Driver Pointer System to search the National Driver Register, a national file of problem drivers reported by all 51 U.S. jurisdictions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
If the search shows you have an unresolved problem in another state, Tennessee cannot issue you a license, even a renewal, until that state's matter is cleared. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Examiners can only tell you which state reported a problem and give a phone number for it; for details you must contact that state, because Tennessee does not hold them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
A Tennessee license may be revoked or suspended for DUI, including refusing a blood alcohol test under implied consent. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
Letting someone else use your license or ID, or fraudulently altering a license, can cost you your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
Leaving the scene of a crash that injures or kills someone, or failing to stop and give aid, is grounds for losing your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
Two reckless driving violations within 12 months, or drag racing, can lead to suspension or revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
Driving away from a gas station without paying for fuel is grounds for losing your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A01
Failing to show proof of insurance or financial responsibility to an officer after a crash or a moving violation charge can lead to suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A01
A driver under 18 can lose driving privileges for any drug or alcohol conviction, whether or not it happened while driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A01
A driver under 18 can lose driving privileges for dropping out of school, failing to make satisfactory progress in school, or carrying weapons on school property. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A01
A suspended or revoked license must be turned in to the Department of Safety within 20 days, and failing to surrender it brings a $75 fine on top of other fines and costs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A01
Before suspending, revoking or canceling a license, the department notifies the driver in writing and offers a hearing, except in cases of final judgments and convictions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A02
You must report a new address to the Department of Safety within 10 days, and you can do it online, by letter or with a form at any Driver License Service Center. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A02
Under the Non-Resident Violator Compact, if you ignore a traffic citation from Tennessee or another member state, your driving privileges will be suspended, revoked or canceled. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A02
A compact suspension lasts until the court tells the department that the citation has been properly handled and the fees are paid. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A02
Every traffic violation or crash on your Department of Safety record carries a point value, based on court reports and officers' crash reports. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A02
An adult driver aged 18 or older who builds up 12 or more points within 12 months receives a notice of proposed suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A02
An adult driver with 6 to 11 points within any 12 months is mailed an advisory letter as a warning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
A juvenile driver under 18 who builds up 6 or more points within 12 months receives a notice of proposed suspension, and one with 1 to 5 points is mailed an advisory letter. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A02
A Defensive Driving Course can help you avoid a point suspension or shorten it, but that option is available only once in any five-year period. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A02
After a suspension for frequent violations, you must pay reinstatement fees and file proof of insurance, with SR-22 insurance required for adults, before getting your regular license back. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A02
Driving while your license is suspended extends the suspension and can lead to criminal prosecution. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A02
A restricted license lets a driver whose license was suspended or revoked, but who needs to drive for work or school, drive only for the specific purposes written on it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A03
Passing a stopped school, church or youth bus that is loading or unloading passengers carries 8 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A03
Failing to stop at a railroad crossing carries 8 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A03
Reckless driving carries 6 points, and careless or negligent driving carries 4 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A03
Using a cell phone while driving under age 18 carries 6 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A03
Failing to yield to emergency vehicles, or failing to change lanes or slow down for authorized vehicles on the roadside, carries 6 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A03
Contributing to a crash that causes property damage carries 3 points, one that causes bodily injury 4 points, and one that causes another person's death 8 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A04
A DUI restricted license is not available to a driver with a prior DUI or adult driving while impaired conviction within 10 years, or a prior vehicular homicide, aggravated vehicular homicide or vehicular assault. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A04
When the department learns that a physical or mental condition affects someone's driving, that driver must send a doctor's medical report within 30 days of being notified. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A04
A driver who loses consciousness or control from epilepsy, cardiac syncope, diabetes or a similar condition must be suspended and stay episode-free for at least six months before reinstatement. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A04
A driver whose ability is in question may be told to take a full or partial driver examination, and ignoring a request for an exam or medical report brings a suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A04
Liability insurance covers damage you cause to others, collision insurance covers damage to your own vehicle, and uninsured motorist insurance covers damage caused by uninsured drivers. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F36 | anchor: A04
Collision insurance is not required in Tennessee, but the Financial Responsibility Law requires you to show proof of financial responsibility whenever you are charged with a violation or are in a crash, whoever was at fault. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-F37 | anchor: A05
Being convicted of failing to show proof of financial responsibility suspends your driving privileges and blocks renewal of your vehicle tags and registration. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F38 | anchor: A05
You must immediately notify local police, or the county sheriff or nearest Highway Patrol outside a city, of any crash causing death, injury or property damage over $50. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F39 | anchor: A05
A crash that kills or injures anyone, or damages any one person's property by more than $400, is a reportable crash that must be reported to the Department of Safety. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F40 | anchor: A05
The driver or owner in a reportable crash must file an Owner/Driver Report with the Department of Safety within 20 days, regardless of who was at fault. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F41 | anchor: A05
Tennessee law requires drivers in a crash to stop immediately at or as near the scene as possible without blocking traffic, and to turn off the ignition to prevent a fire. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F42 | anchor: A05
Do not move an injured person from a wrecked vehicle unless you have medical or rescue training or there is immediate danger such as fire. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-F43 | anchor: A06
If you come upon a crash and are not trained to give aid, call 911 and keep driving slowly past so you do not get in the way of police and rescue crews or cause a secondary collision. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0104]

Misconceptions: Tennessee cannot tell you the details of another state's report; points are not the only way to lose a license, since many single offenses also trigger suspension; collision insurance is optional but proof of financial responsibility is not; the duty to report a crash does not depend on who caused it; stopping to stare at a crash scene is not helpful.
Mnemonics: surrender in twenty, move in ten; twelve points for adults, six for teens; fifty dollars to call police, four hundred to report to the state, twenty days to file.
Glossary: Problem Driver Pointer System means the tool that checks the national register of problem drivers; restricted license means a license limited to stated purposes such as work or school; SR-22 means an insurer's filing that proves liability coverage; reportable crash means one the Department of Safety must receive a written report for.
Dynamic facts: point values, fines, the surrender deadline, reporting dollar thresholds, the Defensive Driving Course limit and restricted license rules are set by Tennessee law and policy and can change; confirm them on official Tennessee sources before showing them to learners.

## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: more suspension grounds, school-related loss for minors, surrender options, address records, reinstatement, speeding points, other point values, restricted license types, medical review, proof of financial responsibility, crash claims, crash-scene information and witnesses
Confusable pairs and continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and any hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
The National Driver Register lists people whose licenses were canceled, denied, revoked or suspended, or who were convicted of certain serious traffic violations. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
Mental or physical conditions that interfere with safe driving, such as Alzheimer's disease, seizures or loss of consciousness, can lead to suspension or revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
Perjury or giving false information about a vehicle's use or ownership or on a license application is grounds for losing your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A01
A felony involving a vehicle, evading arrest while driving, and manslaughter or vehicular homicide are all grounds for revocation or suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A01
Being a habitual recipient of moving violations, or not complying with a court judgment for crash damages, can lead to losing your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A01
Buying or possessing alcohol under age 21, or failing to meet child support requirements, can cost you your license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A01
A driver found with five or more grams of methamphetamine in a vehicle can have the license revoked or suspended. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A01
For the under-18 rule, dropping out means 10 days in a row or 15 total days of unexcused absence in a semester. [A01]
Why it matters: group minors and school; confusable dropping out versus unsatisfactory progress.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A01
For the under-18 rule, satisfactory school progress generally means passing three subjects each grading period. [A01]
Why it matters: group minors and school; confusable unsatisfactory progress versus dropping out.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A01
You can turn in a suspended license at any Tennessee Highway Patrol office or Driver License Service Center to get credit for returning it, or mail it to the department. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A02
Your new address may not appear on the card until a new, renewed or reinstated license is issued, but it must be correct on the official driver license file. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A02
Without a correct address on file you may miss important notices about your license status, and you could be ticketed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A02
Reinstatement steps depend on why you lost your license and what else is on your record, and the department's Financial Responsibility office handles clearing a record. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-R14 | anchor: A02
After a hearing, the department may try education, re-examination, license restrictions and probation to improve poor driving habits before turning to suspension. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec13-R15 | anchor: A03
Speeding 1 to 5 mph over the limit carries 1 point, or 2 points in a construction zone. [A03]
Why it matters: group speeding points; confusable regular versus construction zone.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R16 | anchor: A03
Speeding 6 to 15 mph over the limit carries 3 points, or 4 in a construction zone. [A03]
Why it matters: group speeding points; confusable regular versus construction zone.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R17 | anchor: A03
Speeding 16 to 25 mph over the limit carries 4 points, or 5 in a construction zone. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R18 | anchor: A03
Speeding 26 to 35 mph over carries 5 points, 36 to 45 mph over carries 6, and 46 mph or more over carries 8. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R19 | anchor: A03
Driving below the posted minimum speed or too fast for conditions carries 3 points each. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R20 | anchor: A03
Failing to yield the right of way carries 4 points, and improper passing carries 4 points. [A03]
Why it matters: group yielding points; confusable ordinary yield versus emergency vehicle yield.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R21 | anchor: A03
Following too closely, an improper turn, improper backing and failing to signal each carry 3 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R22 | anchor: A03
Reckless endangerment by vehicle, fleeing a law enforcement officer and child endangerment each carry 8 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R23 | anchor: A03
Driving when the required license is suspended, revoked or canceled carries 8 points, while driving without your license in your possession carries 2 points. [A03]
Why it matters: group license possession points; confusable under suspension versus not carried.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R24 | anchor: A03
Violating the restrictions printed on your license carries 6 points, and failing to report a crash carries 4 points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec13-R25 | anchor: A04
A driver convicted of DUI may get a court-ordered restricted license covering trips such as work, full-time college, worship, probation meetings, treatment programs and interlock appointments. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R26 | anchor: A04
After the first year of a two-year DUI revocation, a driver may apply for a restricted license by installing an ignition interlock for the rest of the revocation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R27 | anchor: A04
An adult suspended for frequent traffic violations may apply to the Driver Improvement Section for a restricted license, with an approval letter, SR-22 proof, tests and fees. [A04]
Why it matters: group restricted licenses; confusable driver improvement versus court order.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R28 | anchor: A04
A person suspended by the court for implied consent, drag racing or a gas drive-off may ask the trial judge for a restricted license for work, full-time college and interlock appointments. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R29 | anchor: A04
A minor who loses a license over drug or alcohol charges may ask the trial judge for a restricted license to drive to and from school or work. [A04]
Why it matters: group restricted licenses; confusable juvenile versus adult.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R30 | anchor: A04
A person suspended for an unsatisfied citation can get a certified court order allowing driving to and from work only, showing the fines paid or a payment plan. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R31 | anchor: A04
If a driver's medical report is unfavorable, the driving privilege stays suspended until the condition improves. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R32 | anchor: A04
The Financial Responsibility Law protects the public from financially irresponsible drivers and from drivers with repeated violations or obvious disregard for traffic laws. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R33 | anchor: A04
Accepted proof of financial responsibility includes your insurance policy declaration page or an insurance binder. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec13-R34 | anchor: A05
Proof of financial responsibility can also be an insurance card from a company authorized in Tennessee, a commissioner's certificate for a cash deposit or bond, or proof of self-insurance. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R35 | anchor: A05
If the driver cannot give the crash notice because of injury, a passenger who is able must make or arrange the notice. [A05]
Why it matters: group crash notice; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R36 | anchor: A05
If a crash involves an unattended vehicle or a domestic animal and you cannot find the owner, report it to the police. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R37 | anchor: A05
Owner/Driver Report forms are available on the Department of Safety website, at any Highway Patrol office, and at any local police station or sheriff's office. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R38 | anchor: A05
Not reporting a crash may lead to suspension of both your driving and registration privileges. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R39 | anchor: A05
When a claim against you is filed with the department, you must show you had liability insurance, get notarized releases from claimants, or post a cash or surety bond, or lose driving and registration privileges. [A05]
Why it matters: group crash claims; confusable three options.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R40 | anchor: A05
You may request an administrative hearing before a financial responsibility revocation if you ask in writing on or before its effective date. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R41 | anchor: A05
If your car is on fire after a crash, help the people out and move them away from the vehicle in case it explodes. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R42 | anchor: A05
Call 911 to report a crash as quickly as possible, and remain calm and stay at the scene. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R43 | anchor: A05
Exchange names, addresses and license numbers with other drivers, and get plate numbers plus the names and addresses of anyone injured and of each witness. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec13-R44 | anchor: A06
Also collect other vehicle owners' names, addresses and insurance policy numbers, and notify your own insurance company right away. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec13-R45 | anchor: A06
If you saw the crash happen, pull safely off the road, turn on your emergency flashers and tell the officer or trooper that you are a witness. [A06]
Why it matters: group crash scene; confusable witness versus passer-by.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec13-R46 | anchor: A06
Secondary crashes near a crash scene are caused by drivers slowing to gaze at it out of curiosity. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0104]

sections.heading: D — Accuracy notes and source flags: driving responsibilities
sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: driving responsibilities
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The whole manual carries an old content-currency date (stated in part A), so any rule here may have changed since; the freshness debt in part A covers every fact in this section.
The points chart was extracted as rows of a value followed by a violation; selected rows were taught as printed, and two garbled rows about operating with or without the required license were not taught (verify TN-RESP-D-POINTS) [A03].
The text points readers to the points chart on a printed page number one lower than the page where the chart actually appears; the chart itself was used [A02].
Crash notice to police is stated with a property-damage threshold in one paragraph and without any threshold a few paragraphs later on the same page; the threshold version is taught (verify TN-RESP-D-NOTICE) [A05].
The study-question answer key printed at the end of this chapter covers every chapter's sample questions; no sample answer is taught as a fact [A06].
Department phone numbers, the mailing address and web addresses are contact details and are not taught.

sections.heading: E — Market signal: driving responsibilities
sections.markdown:
## E — Market signal: driving responsibilities
Market research was not performed in this state worker pass and no CompetitiveIntel artifact was supplied, so the market pack for this topic is typed debt (TN-RESP-MARKET).
Open items: applicant volume, pass rates, seasonality, buyer persona, price expectations, verbatim voice-of-customer quotes, ad hooks and the named gap.
Manual-only observation, not market evidence: learners rarely know the point thresholds and reporting deadlines until they need them, so a what-happens-to-my-license scenario drill is a natural angle to test later.
No market figures are asserted; every figure waits for a sourced recon pass.

sections.heading: E2 — Competitive teardown: driving responsibilities
sections.markdown:
## E2 — Competitive teardown: driving responsibilities
No competitor was reviewed in this pass; names, prices, structure, pedagogy, practice style, praise, complaints and coverage are open (TN-RESP-TEARDOWN).
Adopt and beat lists stay empty until at least two named, priced competitors are examined from their own store or review pages.
Angle to test later: competitors may skip the points chart and reporting thresholds; drilling adult versus teen point limits and the police versus state report duties could be a beat point once verified.

## F — Structured research index and consolidated VERIFY list: driving responsibilities
Knowledge facts: part C holds 43 fact blocks (sec13-F01 onward) from physical pages 99 to 104; part C2 holds 46 confusable and continuation blocks (sec13-R01 onward).
Exam authority: part A states the issuer, the July 1, 2022 content date, the multiple-choice format and its four roughly equal topic areas, the vision standard and the one-day retake wait from physical pages 3, 35 and 36; question count, passing score and time limit are unknown.
VERIFY list:
- TN-RESP-A-EXAM — question count, passing score and time limit not printed in the manual (owner EvidenceLibrarian, official tier).
- TN-RESP-A-FRESH — content dated July 1, 2022; current edition and liveness unconfirmed (owner EvidenceLibrarian, official tier).
- TN-RESP-D-POINTS — points chart rows taught from extracted text; point values need an official recheck (owner EvidenceLibrarian).
- TN-RESP-D-NOTICE — police crash notice with and without a property-damage threshold (owner HallucinationAuditor).

verification_debt.claim_text: The Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual states no question count, passing score or time limit for the Class D knowledge test; an official Department of Safety source is required before any value is shown.

The manual dates its content to July 1, 2022 (physical page 3) and prints a March 2025 authorization on the back cover; no issuer page confirms this as the current edition, so source liveness is unconfirmed and every fact needs a freshness recheck.

Physical page 103 first requires immediate police notice for crashes with death, injury or property damage above a stated dollar amount, then says crashes involving any property damage, injury or death must be reported to police; confirm the current notice requirement.
